text:
Morgan: Heads up — noticed a sharp p95/p99 jump starting ~15:02 UTC right after the runtime v4.3.1 canary flip to 30% traffic. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/p/latency (spike visible on canary cohort).
Jihoon: seeing the same on canary hosts (canary pool 7). p95 ~+180ms, p99 ~+420ms for gen endpoints. No large increase in errors, just tail latency.
Rachel: support has 3 customer tickets flagged as "regression" — customers on dedicated capacity but using the new runtime via version alias. They're noticing slower responses for long-context requests.
Sam: oncall-bot alert came in at 15:04. Can you paste the affected commit list in the rollout? quick hypothesis: scheduler change or quant bump.
oncall-bot: [alert] runtime-p95-surge detected (canary pool 7) threshold exceeded at 2026-03-15T15:03:40Z — link: https://alerts.redwood/runtime-p95-surge
Morgan: rollout diff (v4.3.0 -> v4.3.1): kernel-scheduler:abc123, quant-enc:de4f9, batching-window: default->12ms.
Jihoon: aha the kernel-scheduler patch touched the batch coalescing path and added a small backoff. Could introduce head-of-line for some request sizes.
Sam: can we reproduce locally with synthetic replay? Morgan, can you share a trace id for a slow request?
Morgan: trace ids: trace:6f8a1b, trace:c8d3f0. Flame graph snippets: https://perf.redwood/trace/6f8a1b — shows long wait in scheduler::wait_on_batch_loop.
Rachel: customers report bigger effect on sequences > 1k tokens. Short queries fine.
Sam: repro script (use on a staging canary node):
```bash
# replay a long-context request repeatedly
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rwd-4b","input":"<long prompt padded to 1800 tokens>","max_tokens":512}' https://staging-api.redwood/v1/generate -H "X-Trace-Id: replay-$i" 
done
```
Jihoon: ran 200 replays against 4.3.1 canary pool — reproduced p95 ~+160ms. Re-ran against pinned v4.3.0 -> p95 normal.
Sam: quick mitigation options: 1) route traffic away from v4.3.1 for long-context cohort (route by sequence-length header) 2) reduce batch window from 12ms->6ms for canary 3) pin rollout to exclude kernelscheduler patch. Which do we want now?
Morgan: I'd prefer immediate routing change to buy time. Can we flip routing to send any request with header X-Sequence-Length >= 1024 to v4.3.0? Rachel can notify customers.
Rachel: will update customers and open a status page note. I can mark the three open tickets as "mitigated: routing workaround applied" once done.
Sam: router config snippet to create a simple rule (apply in traffic split service):
```yaml
rules:
  - match: "request.headers['x-sequence-length'] >= 1024"
    action:
      route_to: v4.3.0
      weight: 100
```
Jihoon: applied local test of that rule against canary routing engine and synthetic replay p95 dropped back to baseline. Good sign.
Morgan: I'll roll out the routing rule to prod canary for 30m and monitor. Also starting a targeted bisect plan for the kernel-scheduler patch: disable kernel-scheduler commit (abc123) in a canary build and re-run replays. If that fixes it we have root cause.
Sam: add telemetry check to ensure no impact on overall throughput when reducing batch window — that can increase costs.
Support-ops: logged mitigation action and customer notification: https://status.redwood/incidents/7891 — customers notified 15:28 UTC.
oncall-bot: [job] rollout-change applied: routing-rule v1 by Sam at 15:28:10Z.
Jihoon: bisect results so far: disabling kernel-scheduler patch (build v4.3.1-ks-rollback) on pool 7 drops p99 ~300ms -> baseline. Disabling quant change alone doesn't help. Looks like kernel-scheduler change is the culprit.
Morgan: plan: revert kernel-scheduler change from v4.3.1 and produce v4.3.2 with only safe patches (keep quant-enc and batching-window as-is or tune later). Proposed immediate steps:
- pin long-context routing to v4.3.0 (done)
- cut v4.3.2 without kernel-scheduler commit and deploy to canary pool (Jihoon)
- run synthetic replay and smoke tests (Sam)
- notify customers with ETA for full rollout (Rachel)
Jihoon: preparing v4.3.2 canary build now (CI jobs triggered). Trying to keep batching-window=12ms so we only revert scheduler logic.
Sam: running replay against v4.3.2 canary -> p95/p99 back to baseline on initial 500 runs. Good.
oncall-bot: [deploy] v4.3.2 canary started at 15:46:02Z.
Morgan: after v4.3.2 canary stabilizes for 20m, we can remove the routing rule and resume rollout. Rachel: please hold on customer comms until we have full rollout plan.
Rachel: will post status updates and reply to the 3 tickets. I'll mark one as "escalated" to account team for customer-facing follow up.
Sam: postmortem action items (quick list):
- Add a unit/regression test that exercises the batch coalescing path with long sequences.
- Add a perf alert that watches p95 delta for long-context cohort specifically (compare versions).
- Add a canary gating rule: block kernel-scheduler changes from progressing if long-context p95 increases by >50ms.
Jihoon: also adding a CI perf job that replays a small set of long prompts across PRs touching scheduler.
Morgan: thanks all — mitigation working, will keep monitoring for 2 hours then close thread. Follow-ups: assign owners in the status incident.
Support-ops: incident updated: mitigation applied, canary reverted, v4.3.2 deploying. Will update when routing rule removed.
Rachel: customer update posted at 16:05 UTC. Two customers acknowledged, one asked for postmortem.
Sam: closing notes: root cause = kernel-scheduler backoff behavior interacting badly with long-context batch coalescing. Fix strategy = revert scheduler change + add regression tests + tighten canary gating.
Jihoon: opened PR #5129 with revert and tests.
Morgan: thanks — great cross-team response.
Support-ops: incident resolved, monitoring to continue until 17:30 UTC.
